memory_update.text: WEST is the cleanest Layer 1B underfollowed public candidate for private-label/B2B coffee, tea, extracts, and beverage solutions because official filings map directly to restaurant, foodservice, convenience, hospitality, private-label, and extract/RTD channels.

FARM is a speculative-shadow candidate: strong node relevance through DSD foodservice coffee/tea/beverage route service, but likely micro-cap and high-risk; must verify liquidity, debt, route economics, customer retention, and post-Northlake business mix before promotion.

THS is a broader private-label food and beverage platform with direct coffee capacity via the Farmer Bros Northlake acquisition; useful as a mid-cap private-label beverage reference, but exposure purity may be lower than WEST or FARM.

Need follow-up search for other US-listed or OTC beverage-ingredient, coffee-extract, RTD co-manufacturing, tea, syrup, flavor, and foodservice-equipment suppliers that may be hidden under specialty ingredients or packaged-food classifications.

WEST should remain a priority Layer 2 candidate for the private-label coffee/tea/extract beverage-solutions node because it has direct foodservice/restaurant channel exposure and relatively pure B2B beverage-solutions positioning.

FARM is a high-risk speculative-shadow candidate: direct node relevance via DSD foodservice coffee/beverage service, but market cap, liquidity, balance sheet, and post-divestiture operating stability must be verified before promotion.

THS provides a less pure but more scaled private-label coffee-capacity angle after acquiring Farmer Brothers' Northlake roasting/direct-ship assets; monitor whether coffee category utilization and foodservice channel contribution are material.

Equipment/infrastructure layer is relevant but less direct: MIDD beverage-equipment brands may benefit from restaurant coffee/cold-brew/frozen-beverage program expansion, but the exposure is dispersed and requires segment/backlog/customer-win evidence.

WEST is the highest-quality direct public-market fit for the private-label coffee, tea, extracts, and beverage-solutions node because it explicitly serves foodservice, restaurant, convenience, hospitality, CPG, and private-label/RTD extract use cases.

FARM is a direct but highly speculative micro-cap route-service coffee/tea/foodservice supplier; keep only if later layers verify DSD economics, customer retention, liquidity, and debt/covenant safety.
JVA is a micro-cap speculative-shadow candidate for regional private-label and foodservice coffee exposure; evidence must verify materiality of foodservice/private-label revenue and customer quality.
KDP should be used as a reference benchmark for scaled away-from-home coffee systems, K-Cup manufacturing, and restaurant fountain relationships, not as the underfollowed discovery target.

TreeHouse Foods was historically relevant through the Farmer Brothers coffee asset purchase, but current evidence indicates a completed take-private transaction; exclude from active US-listed universe unless public listing status changes.

Need a later pass for private or non-US comparables in coffee extracts, cold brew concentrates, commercial roasting equipment, beverage QA/testing, and traceability software, because many likely chokepoint assets may not be US-listed.

WEST is the cleanest US-listed small-cap candidate for the private-label coffee, tea, extracts, and B2B beverage-solutions node; next layer should verify customer mix, extract capacity, debt, and free-cash-flow conversion.

FARM is highly node-relevant but should remain speculative_shadow because market cap is far below USD 300M and the post-TreeHouse retained business, customer concentration, liquidity, and delisting/balance-sheet risks require primary-source verification.

THS may hide coffee/private-label beverage exposure inside a broader private-label packaged-food platform after buying Farmer Brothers' non-DSD business and Northlake facility; purity and customer-channel exposure are the main coverage gaps.

The node appears to have very few clean US-listed pure plays above USD 300M; later searches should check Canadian/OTC names, ingredient/extract suppliers, route-service equipment vendors, and restaurant/hospitality beverage distributors, but keep weak names as hypotheses until filings confirm exposure.
